title: Recovery, diet and blowing trumpet again
summary: Punch describes the surgery, his health, daily practice, sitting in on trumpet recently and his diet.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, I wouldn't say they're trying to give me medicine to pass it out, because the doctors were taking extra of me every day and they couldn't find out what we were on. Took me all kind of ways, couldn't find me. They did find out they laid about six or four little pillars, you know? And told me they lay with my back right on them. They took x-ray from the side. They took x-ray from the side. They found out under the liver, the gallstone was under my liver. Oh. It was under there. Oh. And they said I had a pretty dangerous escape there. They had to get under there and cut some of my liver to get to the gallstone. Well, how are you feeling now? Oh, I feel good there now. Other than the high blood pressure now, you're in good shape. Yes, I am. And you're still blowing. You're practicing every other day? Pretty much every day I practice. Do you think that you'll be playing again? The way I feel, I would. The other two Sundays ago, they had a parade way up there, and Adam, in the saloon. And the boys was in there playing. And for some reason, I seen a trumpet laying on the table, you know? And I just couldn't resist. I picked up the trumpet and went to blowing. Everybody started to holler. You blow good? Sure. That's right.
I was there, but I didn't know it was you. You was there?

I blowed like a dog in there, man. Yes, of them. How long did you play? Oh, I must have played about half an hour or more. Is that right? I played about four different tunes. Did you feel any ill effects? Tell me one thing I felt a little dizzy after. I did, I ain't kidding, but they said that's my blood. Yeah. So that's what I got to watch. But down here, nothing. No. Do you eat good? Yeah, I eat heavy. Can you eat anything? No, I have to. You have to watch your diet. Yeah. I see. Yeah, I watch my diet. I don't bother with no kind of salt, no kind of pork. Very little such thing as starch food. You're not ready. When I fix a hamburger, I taste water and put it in the skillet and a little piece of butter and put a lid over it.
Yeah, well you got to watch that diabetes too, you see.

Well, I don't have no trouble with that. I just care of that. You know what I mean? I don't have no trouble with that. Of course, it's dangerous, but I don't have no trouble with it. Yeah, well. Because I've been taking care of it way before I got high up here. Yeah, way before I went to the hospital and I don't have time. Yeah.
